author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Black - PS2 Frame Rate Analysis
summary: NeoGamer measures Criterion’s Black on original PlayStation 2 hardware, using progressive scan and a Retro GEM digital output path to document the actual console frame-rate behavior behind the game’s famously dense effects.

blocks.text: The seven-minute analysis has a tightly defined evidence source: the 2006 PS2 release running on real hardware, captured through a Retro GEM HDMI modification in progressive-scan mode. That makes it useful beside emulator footage because the measured drops and pacing belong to the original console workload rather than a host renderer or speed configuration. Black’s debris, particles, destruction and heavy post-processing make the result a practical reference for what Criterion accepted while pursuing its audiovisual target.

Missing from the metadata are the exact disc region, console revision, capture cadence and analysis software. A digital video modification should not be assumed to alter game simulation merely because it changes the output path. Progressive scan may also differ from the mode many players used historically. The clip establishes a real-hardware performance trace for the scenes shown, not a universal minimum for every mission. Emulator comparisons should match region, video mode and location before treating deviations as correctness defects.
